doc.title: Jimmy Heath — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Opinions on the Obama administration and jazz
summary: Heath hopes President Obama will do something for jazz musicians and starts recalling Cosby's Kennedy Center honor.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: While we’re talking about Washington, just briefly, what are your feelings about this current administration, and are there going to be opportunities for jazz musicians, music?

Well, I think my president has a lot on the table, right now, to get through. He does have, I’ve heard from the grape vine, he does have an advisor, who keeps him up on, and he does know about everybody. Coltrane and everybody; he’s a listener too.
I hear he has a lot of jazz on his iPod.
Yeah. A man of that intelligence; how could he not?
Do you think he put jazz on the iPod he gave to the Queen?
I don’t know. (Laughs) I don’t know.

I’m sure, one he gets past the health thing and all these problems: all these wars, and things; he’ll get around, if he’s still in office, he’ll get around to doing something for us. In fact, I met the first lady. You know, Bill Cosby just did a show at the Kennedy Center where he was honored by…what is it…an award from…
Yeah, I caught a little bit of that. It wasn’t like NAACP or anything right?
Yeah, I know what you’re referring to because I caught just a tiny bit of it.
Do you know, Ken? Ken Kimery: I don’t.
What was it called? He got the award for comedy, what was it called?
